Assistant: Sure, here is a recipe for a typical Latvian dish, frikadeļu zupa or potato soup. To make it, you’d need:

5 kg potatoes

1-2 ltr. water

1 onion (diced)

1 clove garlic (diced)

small amount of salt

2 tbsp butter

1 tbsp flour

1 tbsp flour-dried thyme leaves

1/2 lemon (juice)

grated rind

Some potatoes will need a good washing under cold running water and then put into the pot with water. Bring it up to the boil on a high heat and cook for 40 to 50 minutes or until the potatoes are soft. Then remove and cool.

You can use the whole potato, if that’s what you want. In the meantime, put the butter, the minced garlic and a little salt into the frying pan. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, then put in the onion. Fry for another 3 minutes, then add flour. Add the liquid and stir to mix and thicken. Add flour-dried thyme leaves and stir again. Lower the heat to a mediru setting, and let it simmer about 15 minutes. Put the potato into the pan, and continue cooking until the potatoes are melted and the liquid has all been absorbed. Finally add the rind. Take the pan off the fire and then take the potatoes out of heat.

When the potatoes are cool enough, peel and cut into chunks. Transfer to a large bowl. Then add the lemon juice, mix well. Let it stand for 5 minutes.

When you are ready to serve, take some of the potato soup and add 1 tablespoon of flour to it. You may also add some milk to this to make it more thick in consistency. Add salt and some pepper.

Remove the leaves from the rind. Cut it up into pieces, and serve.
